newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Blackouts loom for electricity customers in W Australia.
newsitem.headline: Blackouts loom for electricity customers in W Australia.

text.p: About 690,000 electricity consumers, including 90,000 businesses, are facing the prospect of blackouts from midnight Thursday because of industrial action by power workers, Western Power said on Thursday.

A Western Power spokesman said an emergency order had been issued under the Electricity Corporation Power Act 1979 which gave Western Power the right to demand all customers reduce consumption "to the absolute minimum".
"The order applies to all customers in the Southwest Interconnected System, even those with contracts which say they cannot have the power cut off," the spokesman said.
"The grid covers everywhere from Kalgoorlie up to Geraldton and down to Albany as well as the Perth metropolitan area."

The spokesman said talks are continuing tonight in the Australian Industrial Relations Commission in a bid to resolve the dispute which arose because of the Government's decision to introduce legislation making several changes to the State's industrial relations laws, including pre-strike secret ballots.
